title: compact cred shim and ergonomic async iterators across python/typescript/go
author: Elias Moreno
release_notes: Introduce compact credential facade and simplified async iterator helpers in Py/TS/Go SDKs. Non-breaking ergonomics and small version bumps. Migration notes included.
description: Motivation: multiple SDKs had similar but diverging credential/stream helper code: repeated warmup paths, heavy factory surface, and inconsistent iterator ergonomics. This PR introduces a compact credential facade that memoizes the most common credential providers (env/KV/kms proxy) and a lightweight async/sync iterator synthesis that brings parity across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Goals: 1) reduce cognitive surface for embedding/stream consumers, 2) standardize retry/warmup semantics for auth exchanges, 3) make incremental migration easy and non-breaking. Summary of changes (single continuous narrative): added a new compact_cred.Facade (py) / CompactCredentialFactory (ts) / credfacade (go) that exposes a small surface: getToken(ctx), warmup(ctx, timeout), and invalidate(). Internally it memoizes the active token provider and performs a background refresh when a refresh window is observed; the background refresh is opt-in via a single configuration flag (enable_background_warmup) to preserve existing behavior. For streaming ergonomics I introduced an AsyncIteratorAdapter for Python and TypeScript and a PullIterator helper for Go; these adapters unify chunked streaming into a single async for / for-await / Next() pattern with consistent cancellation semantics and typed errors. Critically: all changes are guarded with feature flags and fall back to existing factories when the new facade isn't initialized, making this a safe rollout path. Commits: "compact-cred: introduce facade + memoization for env/kv/kms providers"; "sdk-python: async iterator adapter + docs and tests"; "sdk-typescript: CompactCredentialFactory + iterator facade + type fixes"; "sdk-go: credfacade + pull iterator + small API adapters"; "bump: py-sdk 0.17.1, ts-sdk 1.9.3, go-sdk v0.7.2"; "tests: integration harness updates and additional retry scenarios". Changed areas (high-level paths and small snippets): - sdk/python/redwood/compact_cred.py (new): exposes class Facade with methods get_token, warmup, invalidate. Example snippet in codebase: "def get_token(self, ctx): ... # returns Token with expiry" - sdk/typescript/src/credentials/compactFactory.ts (new): export class CompactCredentialFactory { async getToken(ctx) { ... } } - sdk/go/cred/compfacade.go (new): type Facade struct { provider Provider; mu sync.RWMutex } - sdk/*/streaming adapters: added iterator adapter modules and updated consumer examples in examples/streams/simple_consumer.* - docs: docs/sdk/migration/compact-cred.md (new) and docs/sdk/iterators.md (updated) Review summary and major thread: Priya requested that background warmup be opt-in and asked for a clear metric to disable it in case of premature refresh storms — addressed by adding the enable_background_warmup flag and a per-tenant jitter window. Samir flagged a potential race in the Go facade's invalidate path; fixed race by moving to an RWMutex and added a deterministic unit test. Rachel asked for a tighter typed error surface in TypeScript to avoid leaking internal error shapes; updated types and added conversion utilities. Conversation excerpts (condensed): "Priya Nair: please make warmup opt-in and ensure per-tenant jitter (requested change)" — Elias Moreno: "added enable_background_warmup + jitter; updated docs and tests"; "Samir Gupta: possible race in go invalidate() (request change)" — Elias: "switched to RWMutex and added TestInvalidateRace"; "Rachel Kim: prefer TypedAuthError over raw Error in ts (suggested change)" — Elias: "introduced TypedAuthError and conversion helpers". CI: initial run had flaky go unit under TestPullIterator when run with -race on mac builders (CI fail). I reproduced locally and found a small ordering bug in the iterator stop path; fix committed and second CI run passed. Checks: linters (gofmt/eslint/black) passed after fixes, unit tests 100% locally, integration harness exercised cross-sdk flows against staging auth proxy. Merge: merged into main via squash merge on 2026-02-03 after approvals from all reviewers and green CI. Migration / rollout: - step 1: merge behind feature flag (already done) - step 2: deploy SDKs to npm/pypi/goreleaser as patch versions - step 3: enable enable_background_warmup for internal infra tenants, observe warmup metric (auth.background_warmup.invocations) for two weeks - step 4: enable for wider tenants if metrics stable Notes for maintainers: the facade intentionally keeps a tiny API to discourage leakage of provider internals. If you need to add more providers, add them behind the provider registration API in each SDK. If a customer needs hot invalidation semantics at scale, prefer calling invalidate() per tenant rather than disabling memoization. Tests and QA: unit tests added for edge cases (token expiry boundary, mid-stream invalidate), integration tests that exercise retry on transient auth failures, and a short load test showing <3% p99 token latency increase under background_warmup=true on staging. Backwards compatibility: public method names are new but old factories remain exported; no breaking changes expected. Release notes: "SDKs: introduce Compact Credential Facade and ergonomic streaming iterators; non-breaking; patch version bumps. See docs/sdk/migration/compact-cred.md for migration guidance."
